title: Castor (Beaver Wild-Shape) — Reference Plate
source_reconciliation: Use the attached image (Garland holding a beaver) as the definitive source for the beaver form of Castor, the druid in wild-shape — use it for the beaver's appearance (fur, face, tail, paws), but reconcile the pose: in the source the beaver is cradled in a person's arms, so instead render him alone, sitting naturally on his own on the ground. Keep him recognizable as this specific beaver.
identity_lock: An unusually large beaver — about knee-high to a standing person — sitting calmly on his haunches in a natural resting beaver posture, body angled slightly toward the viewer. Rich warm-brown chestnut fur with a slightly paler tan-cream muzzle and cheeks; dark, intelligent, wet-looking eyes; a dark damp nose; small dark rounded ears; prominent rodent incisors; short clawed forepaws; sturdy body; and the classic broad, flat, scaly paddle-tail. Render the specific size cue so his scale reads clearly: he is a large-but-real beaver, knee-high to a person, not a giant. Anatomically true to a real beaver throughout.
image_specific_note: Though he is secretly a sentient druid, he must read as a genuine wild animal: do not let his intelligence become human posture, human expression, or standing/posing like a person. He is calm and candid, not startled or rearing — no action.
